_about: Generated by scripts/sync-trinity-facts.mjs from ivanminier/trinity-site data/facts.json. Do not edit by hand; edit the canonical file and re-sync.

peaks_beds.label: Trinity Peaks beds
peaks_beds.meaning: From the author's room schedule: floors 1-6 hold 1,584 beds (496 singles, 520 doubles, and 16 voluntary triples) and the level-7 loft rooms add about 60 (about 30 in each half). For first- and second-year students. Includes about 36 RA beds; excludes the 4 live-in staff apartments. Not yet tested against a massing study or test fit.

peaks_height.label: Trinity Peaks height
peaks_height.value: Eight levels: a ground level built into the hillside (lobbies, mechanical space, and Northside Dining with its kitchen; no bedrooms), residential floors 1-6 with floor 6 stepping back, and a level 7 that holds only the upper levels of floor-6 lofts and faces inner green-roof courtyards. It reads as about 5-8 stories depending on where it is seen and measured.
peaks_height.meaning: The author's design intent. Height in feet is untested. On the downhill side it would very likely exceed the adopted 55-foot ceiling, so Trinity Peaks would need a zoning amendment as well as Trinity Rise.

rise_beds.label: Trinity Rise beds
rise_beds.meaning: Apartment-style beds for juniors and seniors, built on the land the Back Five halls occupy today, after they are demolished in Phase 2. Built only if Phase 0 and the Phase 2 gate show demand at prices students would choose. Not yet tested at the height target.

rise_height.label: Trinity Rise height target
rise_height.value: 7-10 stories, a modern building with extensive glass and a flat roof
rise_height.meaning: Authored massing target. Height in feet is untested. Illustrative arithmetic (7 floors x 10 ft + 5 ft roof = 75 ft; 10 floors x 12 ft + 6 ft = 126 ft) is well above the adopted 55-foot ceiling, so it would need a zoning amendment; the upper end is also above the tabled 2022 80-foot recommendation, which is not law. Phase 0 would test height and bed count together.

new_beds.label: New-construction beds
new_beds.meaning: Trinity Peaks plus Trinity Rise. New construction only; the retained Cottages (about 30) are not counted.

replacement_beds.label: Existing beds replaced
replacement_beds.meaning: Beds in the halls the plan demolishes: McAuley (about 160) and Mercy (about 182), both from unverified secondary listings, plus the five Back Five halls at 44-45 beds each (220-225, owner-confirmed). Total about 562-567. Broadly consistent with 2022 reporting of roughly 600 students living on Trinity, which may include temporary triples or the Cottages. UVM's designed-bed counts would confirm it. McAuley and Mercy come down in Phase 1B, after the first half of Trinity Peaks opens; the Back Five stay open until Phase 2.

net_new_beds.label: Net-new beds (conditional)
net_new_beds.meaning: Arithmetic result using about 565 replaced beds; it changes if UVM's designed-bed counts differ. It is more than the 1,500 beds the 2023 draft MOU discussed for three UVM parcels together.

peaks_net_new.label: Phase 1 net-new beds (conditional)
peaks_net_new.meaning: Trinity Peaks (1,644) minus McAuley and Mercy (about 342, from unverified listings); the Back Five stay open through Phase 1. A large expansion of first- and second-year beds with no enrollment growth assumed: the demand case must be shown with UVM data, or Peaks gets smaller.

ra_rooms.label: Resident-assistant rooms
ra_rooms.meaning: Three RAs per floor in each half on floors 1-6. RAs are students; their beds are inside the 1,644 Peaks beds.

staff_apartments.label: Live-in staff apartments
staff_apartments.meaning: Four live-in professional staff apartments on floor 1 of Trinity Peaks, two in each half (two one-bedroom and two two-bedroom), each with a full kitchen, living room, washer and dryer, and its own bathroom. Not counted as student beds.

capital_range.label: Planning capital range (order of magnitude)
capital_range.units: USD, escalated to an assumed 2029-2031 construction midpoint
capital_range.meaning: The author's order-of-magnitude planning estimate: gross floor area for each component times a total project cost per square foot (hard cost, soft costs including furniture and equipment, contingency, a LEED premium, and escalation), checked against per-bed benchmarks. It includes the parking garage, Trinity Way and district utilities, demolition, bridge housing, the Cottages, Phase 0, and Trinity Rise. It excludes financing costs, operating costs, and land; off-site utility upgrades beyond the district and replacement of existing surface parking beyond the garage are unknown. Not a professional cost estimate, bid, budget request, or UVM commitment; a cost consultant would replace it in Phase 0. Trinity Rise would be financed by a private partner, not UVM, but it is still part of the district's total cost.

capital_components.label: Capital components
capital_components.value: Phase 0 study $1M-$2M; Trinity Way, utilities, and site $15M-$40M; parking garage $16M-$32M; McAuley and Mercy demolition $4M-$9M; bridge housing $2M-$10M; Trinity Peaks residential $296M-$462M; Northside Dining $30M-$50M; Peaks shared spaces $20M-$34M; Cottages renovation $6M-$12M; Back Five demolition $3M-$7M; Trinity Rise $115M-$258M
capital_components.meaning: Each line is floor area or count times a unit cost, documented in the capital workbook; lines are rounded to $1M and totals are computed before rounding. Phase 1 (Peaks, dining, shared spaces, garage, Trinity Way, demolition, bridge housing, and the Cottages) is $388M-$648M; Phase 2 (Back Five demolition and Trinity Rise) is $118M-$265M; Phase 0 is $1M-$2M.

garage_size.label: Parking garage size
garage_size.meaning: Derived from the author's parking policy: no permits for first-year students, a limited number for sophomores (about 10-20%), permits for about 30-45% of Trinity Rise residents, plus staff, service, and visitors. The number of existing surface spaces the project removes, which may also need replacing, is unknown and would come from UVM Transportation and Parking Services.

per_new_bed.label: District cost per new bed (paired)
per_new_bed.meaning: $507M / 2,144 beds and $914M / 2,344 beds: low cost with the low bed count, high cost with the high. Includes the garage, Trinity Way, the Cottages, and Phase 0. Capital per bed is not rent.

per_net_new_bed.label: District cost per net-new bed (paired)
per_net_new_bed.meaning: $507M / 1,579 and $914M / 1,779. A different metric from cost per new bed; never substitute one for the other.

rise_per_bed.label: Trinity Rise cost per bed
rise_per_bed.meaning: $115M / 500 beds and $258M / 700 beds (paired). A planning figure that a partner's own pro forma would replace.

zoning_current.label: Adopted Trinity Campus overlay rules (as reported)
zoning_current.value: Sec. 4.5.2(e): 40% lot coverage (subject to its stated exception); 115-foot Colchester Avenue buffer; new construction up to the greater of 35 feet or existing structures on the same parcel, with an absolute 55-foot ceiling; institutional parking and major-impact review references
zoning_current.meaning: From the City's Article 4 document marked updated Feb. 10, 2026, as reported by the Oct. 29, 2026 audit and consistent with older ordinance text and the City FAQ. Not a legal review; a planner must confirm intervening amendments.

pc_2022.label: 2022 Planning Commission recommendation
pc_2022.value: 45 feet at the front, 80 feet beyond the existing buffer, 65-foot Colchester Avenue setback, 60% lot coverage
pc_2022.meaning: A Planning Commission recommendation for a zoning amendment, not adopted law. The City Council tabled it on Feb. 21, 2023.

mou_2023.label: December 2023 draft MOU
mou_2023.value: A draft UVM-Burlington memorandum discussed up to 1,500 new beds across three UVM parcels together (Trinity Campus, 280 East Avenue, and the Waterman block), at least 1.5 beds per undergraduate enrolled above the fall 2023 level, and a term through October 2028.
mou_2023.meaning: A historical draft that required City Council approval. It did not allocate 1,500 beds to Trinity. Reporting emphasized upperclass apartment housing. Adoption could not be confirmed in public records searched on Oct. 29, 2026.

mou_status.label: MOU adoption status
mou_status.meaning: Council was expected to take it up on Feb. 12, 2024; no final vote or amendment was found. The two City links previously cited return 404 and are no longer cited.

catamount_woods.label: Catamount Woods
catamount_woods.value: In August 2023 UVM announced about 540 upperclass apartment beds near Centennial Woods with AAM 15, owner of the neighboring DoubleTree hotel, on UVM land already leased to AAM 15 for parking. The early estimate was about $100M (about $185,000 per bed). UVM paused and then halted the project in May 2024 over rising construction costs.
catamount_woods.meaning: The $185,000 figure is a failed early estimate, not an achievable local unit rate. UVM ownership of the land does not by itself permit other uses: current lease terms, partner consent, South Burlington review, utilities, transportation, and restoration would all need confirmation.

bench_vt.label: Virginia Tech benchmark
bench_vt.value: $280M for 1,200 beds (about $233,000 per bed), authorized June 2026, including hard and soft costs
bench_vt.meaning: A different program, region, area, financing, and scope.

bench_unc.label: UNC benchmark
bench_unc.value: roughly $108M-$109M announced for about 700 beds (about $154,000-$156,000 per bed), May 2025
bench_unc.meaning: An announced project budget, not an actual cost and not a Burlington estimate.

trinity_halls.label: Current Trinity housing
trinity_halls.value: UVM's Trinity complex includes McAuley, Mercy, the Cottages, and the Back Five halls (Hunt, McCann, Ready, Richardson, Sichel).

upperclass_options.label: Existing upperclass apartment-style options
upperclass_options.value: UVM-operated residence halls offer traditional and suite-style rooms. Apartment-style options for upperclass students come through UVM-affiliated partner communities, including Redstone Lofts (on UVM's Redstone campus under a ground lease) and University Commons, and Spinner Place in Winooski. Catamount East, which UVM previously leased for juniors, seniors, and transfer students, is no longer a UVM option.
upperclass_options.meaning: Eligibility, prices, and availability vary by community and must be confirmed with UVM. Trinity Rise would add apartment-style capacity at Trinity; whether demand justifies it is a Phase 0 question.

catamount_east.label: Catamount East (lost UVM apartment capacity)
catamount_east.value: Catamount East, a UVM-managed apartment-style building for juniors, seniors, and transfer students at 61 North Dorset St. in South Burlington (about 147-164 beds), is no longer a UVM housing option: UVM's lease with Larkin Realty ended after the 2025-26 year and the units are rented to the public.
catamount_east.meaning: UVM's own apartment-style capacity for upperclass students shrank by roughly 150 beds. This strengthens the case for studying Trinity Rise, but it does not by itself prove demand for 500-700 new beds; Phase 0 must measure that. Bed counts differ by source (147 on UVM's outdated page, 164 in the Vermont Cynic). UVM's Catamount East page has not been updated.

vacancy.label: Rental vacancy
vacancy.meaning: A dated, county-wide (Chittenden County) landlord-survey measure by appraiser Brad Minor. Not a student-only or ZIP 05401 measure.
